title: Enumeration of Bacteria and Cyanobacteria by Flow Cytometry
author: Eric Shimabukuro
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j2wcqfe

steps.title: Collect seawater sample
steps.instruction: Using a 15 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube, collect 10–12 mL of seawater from the Niskin bottle.

steps.title: Fix subsample with paraformaldehyde
steps.instruction: Transfer 2.0 mL of the seawater into a 2 mL Corning cryovial (P/N 66021‑974, VWR) that already contains 30 µL of 16 % paraformaldehyde aqueous solution (Electron Microscopy Sciences Catalog #15700; 15 µL PFA per 1 mL sample).

steps.title: Mix, incubate, freeze sample
steps.instruction: Invert the cryovial 3 times to mix, store in the dark at room temperature for 15 min, then flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and keep at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare sheath fluid system
steps.instruction: Triple‑rinse the sheath fluid reservoir with MilliQ water, then attach a Millipore Sterivex 0.22 µm in‑line filter (P/N SVGPL10RC) to the InFlux sheath‑fluid intake.

steps.title: Set sheath and sample pressures
steps.instruction: Set sheath pressure to 20.0 psi; adjust sample pressure to obtain a flow rate of ≈30 µL min⁻¹ (normally 20.1–20.2 psi). The system uses a Sensirion SLI‑0430 flow meter in‑line between the sample‑line pinch valve and the nozzle, controlled by Spigot software version 6.1.10.0 (Cytopeia).

steps.title: Configure laser sources and alignment
steps.instruction: Activate the 488 nm 200 mW laser (Coherent 488‑200 CRDH) and the 457 nm 300 mW laser (CVI Melles Griot 85‑BLS‑601) at 100 % power. Perform initial alignment with the 488 nm laser, focusing first on the Red and Orange channels then on the FSC channel; subsequently align the 457 nm laser to maximize signal on the Red and FSC channels.

steps.title: Align instrument with fluorescent beads
steps.instruction: Run Spherotech Ultra Rainbow Fluorescent Particles (1.0–1.5 µm, P/N URFP‑10‑5). Adjust gains so that the 1 µm beads cluster near the 10³:1 decade for FSC and Red, the 10¹:5 decade for Orange, and the 10¹:3 decade for Green. Use the following optical filters: FSC – 488 nm blocking; Red – 560 LP > 610 LP > 692/40 BP; Orange – 560 LP > (Reflect) 610 LP > 585/40 BP; Green – (Reflect) 560 LP > 542/27 BP.

steps.title: Stabilize instrument with back flushing
steps.instruction: After final alignment, run the InFlux for 45 min with back‑flushing to stabilize the stream; minor re‑alignments may be needed later.

steps.title: Thaw samples and split aliquots
steps.instruction: Remove frozen samples from –80 °C, place on the bench at room temperature in the dark to thaw. Vortex briefly (<1 s) with a Vortex Genie 2 (Scientific Industries) set to speed 7. Split each 2 mL sample into two 1 mL aliquots in 5 mL polypropylene tubes (P/N 352063, Corning): one for unstained autofluorescence, one for DNA‑stained heterotroph counts. Store the unstained aliquots at 4 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Add beads to unstained aliquots
steps.instruction: Prepare a bead dilution by adding 2 drops of URFP‑10‑5 beads to 3 mL MilliQ water in a PP tube and vortex briefly. Add 2 µL of this dilution to each unstained 1 mL aliquot, vortex ≈2 s, and keep the samples at 4 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Prepare SYBR Green I working dilution
steps.instruction: Retrieve the 10 000× SYBR Green I stock (Lonza, P/N 50513) from the –20 °C freezer, place on ice to thaw, and centrifuge 20 s to condense. Make a 200× working dilution by mixing 20 µL stock with 980 µL MilliQ water filtered through a 0.1 µm Acrodisc syringe filter (VWR P/N 28143‑309) to a final volume of 1000 µL; vortex briefly. The working stock (50‑fold dilution of the original concentrate) is stable at room temperature for 1 day, at 4 °C for up to 5 days, and at –20 °C for ≥1 month. Use sterile/DNA‑free consumables.

steps.title: Add SYBR stain to stained aliquots
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of the 200× SYBR Green I working dilution to each stained (heterotroph) 1 mL aliquot and vortex ≈2 s.

steps.title: Incubate stained samples at 4°C
steps.instruction: Place all SYBR‑stained aliquots in a 4 °C refrigerator for 20 min; keep them at 4 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Set FSC trigger and run unstained sample
steps.instruction: Configure the InFlux to trigger on FSC with a trigger level of 10–20. Place the PP tube containing the unstained sample on the sampler, press Run, and allow the sample to equilibrate for ≥30 s until event plots in Spigot are stable. Stop the run. (Optional: remove the tube and record its initial mass for a mass‑difference flow calculation.)

steps.title: Backflush sample line between runs
steps.instruction: After each sample run, back‑flush the InFlux sample line for ≥30 s before the next sample.

steps.title: Switch to Green trigger for stained samples
steps.instruction: Change the trigger channel to Green with a trigger level of 40–50. Prepare the stained samples as described in steps 9–12, ensuring they have rested in the refrigerator for at least 20 min before analysis.

steps.title: Run stained sample analysis
steps.instruction: Begin list‑file collection in Spigot, reset the Totalizer on the SLI‑0430 software, press Run, and collect data until the flow meter records 100 µL of sample having passed. Stop the run and, if desired, weigh the tube.

steps.title: Clean instrument when using SYBR
steps.instruction: Before any SYBR‑Green run, flush the sample line sequentially with 5 % CONTRAD 70 detergent, then 70 % ethanol, then MilliQ water until the FSC event rate falls below 20.

steps.title: Repeat unstained run with reduced volume
steps.instruction: Repeat the unstained‑sample procedure (steps 9–14) but set the analysis volume to 50 µL instead of 100 µL.

steps.title: Analyze data in FlowJo
steps.instruction: Open the .fcs files in FlowJo version 10.2. Gate populations as follows: Prochlorococcus – Red vs FSC > Orange vs FSC; Synechococcus – Green vs Orange > Orange vs FSC; Pico‑Eukaryotes – Red vs FSC > Orange vs FSC; Heterotrophs (SYBR‑stained) – Green vs FSC. For heterotroph counts, subtract the Prochlorococcus count (both take up SYBR and have overlapping FSC/SSC).

steps.title: Calculate cell concentrations with corrections
steps.instruction: Convert raw counts to cells mL⁻¹ by dividing each count by the corrected sample volume. Correct volumes: unstained samples ÷ 1.017 (accounts for 15 µL PFA + 2 µL beads); stained samples ÷ 1.020 (accounts for 15 µL PFA + 5 µL stain). Convert to seawater volume using the static coefficient 0.0009718 (derived from seawater density 1.026 µg µL⁻¹) in the mass‑difference method.
